## The question behind the headline {.smaller}

Between 2003 and 2024, the median age at first marriage in Singapore rose from 29.1 to 31.1 for grooms and from 26.6 to 29.6 for brides [@singstat_m830169].
Among those who remarry, the shift is larger still.

::: box
Singaporeans are not rejecting marriage.
They are **delaying** it, and who delays the most is changing.
:::

Three questions drive our project:

- How wide is the gap between first-marriage and re-marriage age, and has it grown?
- Are grooms and brides changing at the same pace, or is one moving faster?
- Can a single interactive chart carry all of that without asking the reader to track four lines at once?

::: small
Data: Singapore Department of Statistics, Table M830169.
Original reporting: Mothership.SG (15 July 2024) [@mothership2024].
:::

## The original visualization {.smaller}

The chart appeared in a Mothership.SG article on Singapore's 2023 marriage and divorce figures, written for a general audience [@mothership2024].
It plots four series from 2003 to 2023.

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
![Original static four-line chart, Mothership.SG (2024), sourced from SingStat.](https://static.mothership.sg/1/2024/07/Screenshot-2024-07-15-at-7.46.14%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
**The story it tells**

All four lines climb across twenty years.
Re-marriage sits roughly ten to fourteen years above first marriage throughout.

The broad message lands in a glance: people are marrying later, first marriage or not.
:::
:::::

::: small
Grooms and brides, at first marriage and re-marriage.
Median age on the y-axis, year on the x-axis.
:::

## What the original does well {.smaller}

::: box
Four dimensions in one plot: **year** (x-axis), **median age** (y-axis), **gender** (colour), **marriage type** (line style).
No flipping between charts.
:::

- **Solid versus dashed reads intuitively.** A dashed line for re-marriage follows a visual grammar most readers already know, so the two marriage types separate without constant legend checks.
- **Direct data labels remove guesswork.** Values are printed beside plotted points, which matters for a static image with no hover tooltip to fall back on.
- **The warm colour pairing stays coherent.** Red for grooms and orange for brides read as one family with two variants, suiting two genders inside one institution.

A non-specialist takes in the headline, that people marry later, within a few seconds.

## Where it falls short {.smaller}

| \# | Weakness |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **W1** | The two closely spaced line pairs are hard to tell apart; the eye keeps returning to the legend |
| **W2** | The gender comparison readers want is buried under two encodings at once |
| **W3** | Only four points across twenty years, unevenly spaced, so most of the series is invisible, and the static format can't answer "what was the value in 2017?" either |
| **W4** | Median age is the only statistic shown; there's no sense of spread, so readers can't tell whether that "typical" age represents most couples or hides a wide range |
| **W5** | The most interesting number, the closing gender gap, is never shown |
| **W6** | Red and orange sit close for readers with colour vision deficiency |

::: small
One root cause: a detailed dataset served through a format, four overlapping lines with four labelled points, that cannot show gaps, trends, distributions, or intermediate values without work from the reader.
W3 folds together what were originally two separate points (sparse points, and no way to look up a value); on review they were really one problem with two symptoms, so we merged them.
:::

## Our redesign: an interactive dumbbell {.smaller}

Each bar spans one year, from the first-marriage age to the re-marriage age, so the **gap becomes the visual subject** rather than something the reader calculates.
A gender toggle shows one set of dumbbells at a time, and hovering any year now opens a linked view of how that year's ages were actually distributed.

| Fixes | Improvement |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| **W1, W2** | Dumbbell layout toggled by gender, so no second pair of lines competes for attention |
| **W3** | Every year from 2003 to 2024 plotted, and hovering (not clicking) any row surfaces its exact values, both endpoints labelled for all 22 years |
| **W4** | A linked distribution panel: for the year under the pointer, it plots the full age-band histogram plus the mean and the mode, not just the single median line the original relies on |
| **W5** | The numeric gap printed on every connector |
| **W6** | An interactive toggle; only one gender's colour is ever on screen |

::: small
The linked distribution panel draws on SingStat's age-band counts, which are published for all marriage orders combined rather than split by first marriage versus re-marriage [@singstat_m830103].
It describes the overall population for that year, not the first-marriage or re-marriage series specifically.
:::

```{=html}

    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="display:flex;gap:14px;align-items:flex-start;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center;">
    <div style="flex:1 1 600px;min-width:480px;">
      <div id="db-legend" style="display:flex;gap:22px;padding:0 8px 2px;font-size:13px;color:#5f6b7a;flex-wrap:wrap;"></div>
      <div id="db-chart" style="width:100%;max-height:66vh;overflow-y:auto;overflow-x:hidden;"></div>
    </div>
    <div style="flex:0 0 380px;">
      <div id="dist-title" style="font-family:Inter,sans-serif;font-weight:600;font-size:13px;color:#23304a;padding:4px 0 2px;">

      </div>
      <div id="dist-chart" style="width:100%;"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="small" style="padding:4px 8px 4px;font-size:12px;color:#8a8577;">
    Source: Singapore Department of Statistics, Tables M830169 (median ages) and M830169 (age-band counts).
    Number on each bar is the gap in years. Covid-affected marriage years, 2020&ndash;2021, fall inside the range shown.
    Age-band counts for 2024 are not yet published by SingStat, so the distribution panel has no 2024 option even though the dumbbell does.
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA=MARRIAGE_DATA; // shared source, defined once in the deck's <head>

  var AGE_BANDS=["Under 20","20-24","25-29","30-34","35-39","40-44","45-49","50-54","55-59","60 & Over"];
  var BAND_MID=[18,22.5,27.5,32.5,37.5,42.5,47.5,52.5,57.5,65];
  var GROOM_BANDS={2003:[139,2103,8923,5613,2476,1323,714,373,179,119],2004:[129,2138,8259,5812,2665,1492,851,480,200,163],2005:[120,2056,7936,5960,2873,1795,1108,607,314,223],2006:[125,1985,8505,6327,2929,1613,1064,610,312,236],2007:[116,1899,8468,6398,3040,1771,1078,610,347,239],2008:[130,1823,8847,6510,3216,1768,1052,623,361,266],2009:[106,1783,9378,6923,3486,1800,1162,728,391,324],2010:[99,1696,8297,6686,3310,1746,1154,673,397,305],2011:[101,1698,9275,7771,3679,1842,1221,815,473,383],2012:[84,1907,9429,8012,3744,1907,1201,794,438,420],2013:[81,1675,8745,7765,3508,1826,1094,766,425,369],2014:[70,1625,9834,8444,3697,2053,1090,764,456,374],2015:[72,1534,9698,8524,3689,2024,1106,747,486,442],2016:[52,1415,9838,8359,3681,1941,1076,700,439,470],2017:[58,1376,10494,8102,3623,1925,1047,690,464,433],2018:[40,1295,9722,7891,3579,1757,1099,699,465,460],2019:[53,1129,8623,7795,3471,1665,1033,659,492,514],2020:[40,1127,7841,7242,2990,1409,854,490,324,334],2021:[32,1229,9759,9899,3716,1570,830,545,374,375],2022:[38,1134,9501,10133,3873,1812,1043,741,513,601],2023:[40,976,8630,9725,3883,1938,1125,767,552,674]};
  var BRIDE_BANDS={2003:[620,5639,9798,3539,1254,616,318,114,49,15],2004:[683,5493,9450,3868,1441,668,354,140,58,34],2005:[731,5331,9634,4216,1645,770,398,165,69,33],2006:[636,5114,10317,4479,1681,825,377,158,81,38],2007:[643,4791,10528,4680,1825,819,399,186,62,33],2008:[562,4699,11013,4798,1900,890,421,187,83,43],2009:[503,4770,11773,5226,2117,846,462,228,110,46],2010:[471,4192,10748,5185,2065,812,509,243,87,51],2011:[408,4444,12123,5972,2266,1069,528,280,99,69],2012:[386,4622,12213,6308,2358,1071,542,244,115,77],2013:[355,4030,11428,6134,2347,1027,517,241,114,61],2014:[286,4042,12820,6704,2390,1127,566,287,117,68],2015:[278,3772,12763,6713,2501,1183,582,310,121,99],2016:[244,3448,12945,6574,2511,1141,595,292,126,95],2017:[204,3259,13361,6490,2595,1145,623,295,144,96],2018:[159,2997,12467,6464,2555,1119,655,327,154,110],2019:[146,2611,11143,6573,2540,1123,661,343,170,124],2020:[134,2394,9992,5967,2241,915,499,274,137,98],2021:[123,2661,12458,8263,2682,1019,526,324,138,135],2022:[135,2462,12244,8654,2998,1305,775,425,218,173],2023:[111,2113,11374,8509,3180,1475,715,455,197,181]};

  var PAL={
    groom:{first:'#7b9acc',remar:'#2f4b7c',line:'#b9c6dd',label:'Grooms',title:'#2f4b7c',bandKey:GROOM_BANDS,imgFirst:'assets/groom-1st.png',imgRemar:'assets/groom-2nd.png'},
    bride:{first:'#d98fae',remar:'#a8456b',line:'#eccddb',label:'Brides',title:'#a8456b',bandKey:BRIDE_BANDS,imgFirst:'assets/bride-1st.png',imgRemar:'assets/bride-2nd.png'}
  };
  // Mean/mode colours, contrast-checked directly against the bars they sit
  // on (WCAG 1.4.11, >=3:1 for graphical objects) -- not against the page
  // background. A mid-tone hue can't clear 3:1 against both the groom bar
  // (#2f4b7c) and the bride bar (#a8456b) at once (their luminance is too
  // close together for that), so both marks use a bright, light colour
  // instead -- that's the only way to get real separation from either bar
  // without relying on a halo. Because a colour that bright reads poorly as
  // *text* on the white/#faf8f4 legend strip, the legend labels ("Mean",
  // "Mode") stay in the deck's normal dark text colour; only the small
  // swatch/line next to each label, and the marks inside the chart, use
  // MEAN_COLOR/MODE_COLOR.
  var MODE_COLOR='#5fe0c0'; // bright mint: 5.3:1 vs groom bar, 3.5:1 vs bride bar
  var MEAN_COLOR='#ffd34d'; // bright gold: 6.1:1 vs groom bar, 3.9:1 vs bride bar
  var LEGEND_TEXT='#23304a'; // deck's standard dark text colour, used for legend labels instead of MEAN_COLOR/MODE_COLOR
  // The SVG has width="100%" and no fixed CSS height, so its rendered size on screen
  // is (container width) x (container width * H/W) -- W/H below are a coordinate
  // system and aspect ratio, not literal on-page pixels. Making rows taller/icons
  // bigger is done by raising H relative to W (a taller aspect ratio at the same
  // container width), not by inflating W -- growing W just made the *columns* flex
  // item request more horizontal space than the slide actually had, which is what
  // pushed the layout into flex-wrap and knocked the distribution panel below the
  // fold with no way to scroll back to it. Container width is controlled separately,
  // by the flex-basis values on the two columns below.
  var W=1000,H=820,mL=60,mR=48,mT=60,mB=30,iw=W-mL-mR,ih=H-mT-mB,AMIN=25.3,AMAX=46.6;
  var IMG_R=15; // half-width/height of the endpoint images (was circle r=5, then 9, then 11).
  // Row height is ih/n =~33px, so a 30px-diameter image still clears its neighbours; going
  // any bigger than this starts crowding adjacent rows in a 22-row chart.
  function xs(a){return mL+(a-AMIN)/(AMAX-AMIN)*iw;}
  var n=DATA.length,rowH=ih/n;
  function yr(i){return mT+rowH*i+rowH/2;}
  var COVID=[2020,2021];
  var currentGender='groom';
  var hoverYear=2023;

  function esc(v){return v.toFixed(1);}

  function draw(g){
    currentGender=g;
    var p=PAL[g];
    var s='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+W+' '+H+'" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Dumbbell chart of median marriage age" style="font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">';
    for(var a=26;a<=46;a+=2){var gx=xs(a);s+='<line x1="'+gx+'" y1="'+(mT-6)+'" x2="'+gx+'" y2="'+(H-mB+4)+'" stroke="#eee6d8"/>';s+='<text x="'+gx+'" y="'+(mT-12)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#9aa2ad">'+a+'</text>';}
    s+='<text x="'+(mL+iw/2)+'" y="16" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#5f6b7a">Median age (years)</text>';
    for(var i=0;i<n;i++){
      var d=DATA[i],yy=yr(i);
      var x1=xs(g==='groom'?d.gf:d.bf),x2=xs(g==='groom'?d.gr:d.br);
      var v1=(g==='groom'?d.gf:d.bf),v2=(g==='groom'?d.gr:d.br),gap=v2-v1;
      var isC=COVID.indexOf(d.y)>-1;
      var isHover=(d.y===hoverYear);
      s+='<rect x="0" y="'+(yy-rowH/2)+'" width="'+W+'" height="'+rowH+'" fill="'+(isHover?'rgba(181,101,29,0.08)':'transparent')+'" class="db-row" data-year="'+d.y+'"/>';
      s+='<text x="'+(mL-14)+'" y="'+(yy+4)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="12.5" fill="'+(isC?'#b5651d':'#5f6b7a')+'" font-weight="'+(isC?'700':'500')+'">'+d.y+'</text>';
      s+='<line x1="'+x1+'" y1="'+yy+'" x2="'+x2+'" y2="'+yy+'" stroke="'+p.line+'" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"/>';
      s+='<text x="'+((x1+x2)/2)+'" y="'+(yy-7)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#7a8494" font-weight="600">'+gap.toFixed(1)+'</text>';
      // Endpoint markers: a small "1st"/"2nd" marriage badge icon per gender, in place of a plain circle.
      // Expects assets/groom-1st.png, assets/groom-2nd.png, assets/bride-1st.png, assets/bride-2nd.png
      // saved alongside this .qmd (same size square PNGs; scaled here to 2*IMG_R).
      s+='<image href="'+p.imgFirst+'" x="'+(x1-IMG_R)+'" y="'+(yy-IMG_R)+'" width="'+(2*IMG_R)+'" height="'+(2*IMG_R)+'"/>';
      s+='<image href="'+p.imgRemar+'" x="'+(x2-IMG_R)+'" y="'+(yy-IMG_R)+'" width="'+(2*IMG_R)+'" height="'+(2*IMG_R)+'"/>';
      s+='<text x="'+(x1-IMG_R-4)+'" y="'+(yy+4)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="11.5" fill="'+p.first+'" font-weight="600">'+esc(v1)+'</text>';
      s+='<text x="'+(x2+IMG_R+4)+'" y="'+(yy+4)+'" text-anchor="start" font-size="11.5" fill="'+p.remar+'" font-weight="700">'+esc(v2)+'</text>';
    }
    s+='</svg>';
    document.getElementById('db-chart').innerHTML=s;
    document.getElementById('db-legend').innerHTML='<span><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:'+p.first+';margin-right:6px;"></span>First marriage</span><span><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:'+p.remar+';margin-right:6px;"></span>Re-marriage</span>';
    var gEl=document.getElementById('db-gender');gEl.textContent=p.label;gEl.style.color=p.title;
    document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').className=(g==='groom'?'active-groom':'');
    document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').className=(g==='bride'?'active-bride':'');

    // hover on a row selects its year for the linked distribution panel
    var rows=document.querySelectorAll('#db-chart .db-row');
    rows.forEach(function(r){
      r.addEventListener('mouseenter',function(){
        hoverYear=Number(r.getAttribute('data-year'));
        draw(currentGender);
        drawDist();
      });
    });
    drawDist();
  }

  function weightedMean(counts){
    var num=0,den=0;
    counts.forEach(function(c,i){num+=c*BAND_MID[i];den+=c;});
    return num/den;
  }
  function modeIndex(counts){
    var best=0;
    counts.forEach(function(c,i){if(c>counts[best])best=i;});
    return best;
  }

  function drawDist(){
    var title=document.getElementById('dist-title');
    var target=document.getElementById('dist-chart');
    var p=PAL[currentGender];
    var counts=p.bandKey[hoverYear];
    var DW=410,DH=500,pL=30,pR=10,pT=16,pB=48; // bumped up alongside the dumbbell canvas below

    if(!counts){
      title.textContent='Age-band distribution: not published for '+hoverYear;
      target.innerHTML='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+DW+' '+DH+'" width="100%"><text x="'+(DW/2)+'" y="'+(DH/2)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#8a8577" font-family="Inter,sans-serif">SingStat has not released 2024 age-band counts yet</text></svg>';
      return;
    }
    title.textContent='Age-band distribution, '+p.label.toLowerCase()+', '+hoverYear+' (all marriage orders combined)';

    var maxCount=Math.max.apply(null,counts);
    var mean=weightedMean(counts);
    var mI=modeIndex(counts);
    var xMin=15,xMax=70;
    var legendH=26; // reserved strip at the top for the Mean/Mode legend, kept clear of the bars
    function x(age){return pL+(age-xMin)/(xMax-xMin)*(DW-pL-pR);}
    var barW=(x(BAND_MID[1])-x(BAND_MID[0]))*0.6;
    var yBase=DH-pB,yTop=pT+legendH;
    function y(c){return yBase-(c/maxCount)*(yBase-yTop);}

    var s='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+DW+' '+DH+'" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Age-band distribution" style="font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">';

    // legend row: swatch colour is MEAN_COLOR/MODE_COLOR (matches the in-chart marks, so it
    // reads clearly against the bars); the label text stays in the deck's normal dark colour,
    // since a colour bright enough to clear the bars reads poorly as small text on this white strip.
    s+='<line x1="'+pL+'" y1="'+(pT+6)+'" x2="'+(pL+18)+'" y2="'+(pT+6)+'" stroke="'+MEAN_COLOR+'" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>';
    s+='<text x="'+(pL+23)+'" y="'+(pT+9)+'" font-size="9.5" fill="'+LEGEND_TEXT+'" font-weight="700">Mean '+mean.toFixed(1)+'</text>';
    s+='<rect x="'+(pL+90)+'" y="'+pT+'" width="12" height="12" fill="'+MODE_COLOR+'" stroke="none"/>';
    s+='<text x="'+(pL+107)+'" y="'+(pT+9)+'" font-size="9.5" fill="'+LEGEND_TEXT+'" font-weight="700">Mode</text>';

    AGE_BANDS.forEach(function(band,i){
      var cx=x(BAND_MID[i]);
      var barH=yBase-y(counts[i]);
      var isMode=(i===mI);
      s+='<rect x="'+(cx-barW/2)+'" y="'+y(counts[i])+'" width="'+barW+'" height="'+barH+'" fill="'+p.remar+'" opacity="'+(isMode?1:0.85)+'" stroke="'+(isMode?MODE_COLOR:'none')+'" stroke-width="'+(isMode?3:0)+'"/>';
      s+='<text x="'+cx+'" y="'+(yBase+13)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="8" fill="#6b7480" transform="rotate(28 '+cx+' '+(yBase+13)+')">'+band+'</text>';
    });
    var meanX=x(mean);
    // Mean line: bright gold, drawn directly over the bars -- no halo. At stroke-width 2.4 it
    // clears 3:1 against both the groom-blue and bride-mauve bar fills on its own (see the note
    // above MEAN_COLOR/MODE_COLOR for the actual ratios).
    s+='<line x1="'+meanX+'" y1="'+yTop+'" x2="'+meanX+'" y2="'+yBase+'" stroke="'+MEAN_COLOR+'" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-dasharray="5,3"/>';
    s+='<line x1="'+pL+'" y1="'+yBase+'" x2="'+(DW-pR)+'" y2="'+yBase+'" stroke="#e4e0d8"/>';
    s+='</svg>';
    target.innerHTML=s;
  }

  document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').addEventListener('mouseenter',function(){draw('groom');});
  document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').addEventListener('mouseenter',function(){draw('bride');});
  document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').addEventListener('click',function(){draw('groom');});
  document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').addEventListener('click',function(){draw('bride');});

  draw('groom');
})();
</script>
```

## From raw export to clean table {.smaller}

The SingStat file is not a clean rectangle.
Ten metadata rows precede the table, marriage type and sex are implied by row text and indentation, and year headers carry trailing whitespace.
Five sequential stages resolve this.

```{=html}
<svg width="100%" height="150" viewBox="0 0 900 150" style="display:block;margin:0.4rem auto;">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="6" refY="4" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z" fill="#5f6b7a"></path>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  ${""}
  <rect x="10" y="55" width="160" height="46" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="1.4"></rect>
  <text x="90" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="700">1. Import</text>
  <text x="90" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Read raw CSV</text>

  <rect x="188" y="55" width="160" height="46" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="1.4"></rect>
  <text x="268" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="700">2. Baseline check</text>
  <text x="268" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Record raw shape</text>

  <rect x="366" y="55" width="160" height="46" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="1.4"></rect>
  <text x="446" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="700">3. Label</text>
  <text x="446" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Tag type and gender</text>

  <rect x="544" y="55" width="160" height="46" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="1.4"></rect>
  <text x="624" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="700">4. Reshape and filter</text>
  <text x="624" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Pivot long, keep rows we need</text>

  <rect x="722" y="55" width="160" height="46" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="1.4"></rect>
  <text x="802" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="700">5. Gap and schema</text>
  <text x="802" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Compute gaps, validate, write</text>

  <line x1="170" y1="78" x2="186" y2="78" stroke="#5f6b7a" stroke-width="1.4" marker-end="url(#arrow)"></line>
  <line x1="348" y1="78" x2="364" y2="78" stroke="#5f6b7a" stroke-width="1.4" marker-end="url(#arrow)"></line>
  <line x1="526" y1="78" x2="542" y2="78" stroke="#5f6b7a" stroke-width="1.4" marker-end="url(#arrow)"></line>
  <line x1="704" y1="78" x2="720" y2="78" stroke="#5f6b7a" stroke-width="1.4" marker-end="url(#arrow)"></line>
</svg>
```

| Stage | Action |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **1. Import** | Read the CSV, skip ten metadata rows, keep the year headers as a separate vector |
| **2. Baseline check** | Record raw dimensions, missing cells, and year range as a reference to reconcile against |
| **3. Label** | Tag each row from its text using the `" - "` delimiter, carry type and sex onto indented rows |
| **4. Reshape and filter** | Pivot long, then filter to Total Marriages, first and re-marriage, year ≥ 2003 |
| **5. Gap and schema** | Pivot wide, compute `groom_gap` and `bride_gap`, validate row count and plausibility |

::: small
Each stage reads the output of the one before and produces a new object, so any single step stays inspectable and re-runnable on its own.
:::

## The pipeline in code {#pipeline-code .smaller}

The same five stages as the previous slide, now as five separate, foldable code chunks.

**Stage 1 · Import**

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
library(tidyverse) # <1>

raw <- read_csv("data/raw/M830169_raw.csv", skip = 10, col_names = FALSE) # <2>
years_header <- raw |> slice(1) |> select(-1) |> unlist() |> as.numeric() # <3>
```

1.  `tidyverse` bundles `readr`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `stringr`, everything the rest of the pipeline calls on.
2.  Skips the ten metadata rows above the actual table; `col_names = FALSE` keeps the raw layout so row 1 can still be read as data rather than headers.
3.  Row 1 holds the year labels (2003…2025). Pulled out now and kept as a separate vector, since Stage 3 reattaches it explicitly as column names.

**Stage 2 · Baseline check**

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
baseline <- list(
  n_rows    = nrow(raw),      # <1>
  n_missing = sum(is.na(raw)) # <2>
)
```

1.  Row count taken straight off the untouched import, before any filtering or reshaping.
2.  Missing-cell count recorded here too, so Stage 5's checks have a known-good reference to compare against.

**Stage 3 · Label**

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
marriage <- raw |> slice(-1) |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(X1),                                          # <1>
         is_header = str_detect(label, " - "),                          # <2>
         type   = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 1), NA), # <3>
         gender = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 2), NA)) |>
  fill(type, gender, .direction = "down") |>                            # <4>
  mutate(order = if_else(is_header, "All", label)) |>                   # <5>
  set_names(c("X1","label","is_header","type","gender","order", years_header)) # <6>
```

1.  Drops the header row consumed in Stage 1, then trims stray whitespace from every remaining row label.
2.  Header rows read like `"Total Marriages - Grooms"`; the `" - "` delimiter is what tells a header row apart from an indented data row.
3.  `str_split_i` reads the marriage type and gender straight out of that header label.
4.  Indented data rows (e.g. `"First Marriages"`) carry no type/gender of their own, so `fill()` carries the last header's values down onto them.
5.  Header rows get `order = "All"`; every other row keeps its own label (`"First Marriages"`, `"Remarriages"`, …) as the marriage order.
6.  Reattaches the `years_header` vector from Stage 1 as the real column names, replacing the placeholder `V2, V3, …` names.

**Stage 4 · Reshape and filter**

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
marriage <- marriage |>
  pivot_longer(-c(X1,label,is_header,type,gender,order),
               names_to = "year", values_to = "age") |>                 # <1>
  filter(type == "Total Marriages",                                     # <2>
         order %in% c("First Marriages","Remarriages"),                 # <3>
         as.integer(year) >= 2003) |>                                   # <4>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(gender, order), values_from = age)         # <5>
```

1.  One column per year becomes one row per year; every later step, and every chart on this slide, assumes long format.
2.  Keeps only the combined-order total, dropping the by-citizenship and by-ethnicity breakdowns the raw file also carries.
3.  Restricts marriage order to first marriages and remarriages, the two series the dumbbell chart needs.
4.  Matches the 2003–2024 window used throughout the deck, so it lines up with the year the original chart starts.
5.  Pivots back to wide, keyed this time on gender and order, so `groom_first`, `groom_remarry`, `bride_first`, and `bride_remarry` each become their own column.

**Stage 5 · Gap and schema**

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"
marriage <- marriage |>
  mutate(groom_gap = groom_remarry - groom_first,                       # <1>
         bride_gap = bride_remarry - bride_first)

stopifnot(nrow(marriage) == 22,                                         # <2>
          all(marriage$groom_gap > 0, marriage$bride_gap > 0),          # <3>
          n_distinct(marriage$year) == nrow(marriage))                  # <4>

write_csv(marriage, "data/clean/M830169_cleaned.csv")                   # <5>
```

1.  The gap columns are computed once, here, so every chart and analysis slide downstream reads the same number instead of recomputing it inline.
2.  Confirms the row count matches the expected 22 years (2003–2024) before the file is trusted downstream.
3.  Re-marriage age should always exceed first-marriage age; this fails loudly if a join or filter went wrong upstream.
4.  Guards against a duplicated year slipping through the pivot undetected.
5.  Writes the cleaned, validated table that every other slide in this deck reads from.

## A1: Brides' First-Marriage Age Rises Twice as Fast {.smaller}

A linear regression of first-marriage age on year, fitted separately per gender.

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: box
**Brides rise about twice as fast as grooms, and both slopes are significant.**

Brides: **0.14 years/year** (95% CI 0.13–0.14; R² 0.98; *p* \< .001)

Grooms: **0.07 years/year** (95% CI 0.06–0.08; R² 0.87; *p* \< .001)
:::

Over 2003 to 2024, that is a gain of about **3.0 years** for brides against **2.0 years** for grooms.
A direct test of the two slopes (Welch-style *t*-test on the difference) confirms the gap in *rates* itself is significant: *t*(40) = 9.89, *p* \< .001.
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div id="a1-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA=MARRIAGE_DATA; // shared source, defined once in the deck's <head>; this chart only reads .y/.gf/.bf
  var W=480,H=180,mL=34,mR=14,mT=26,mB=26,iw=W-mL-mR,ih=H-mT-mB;
  var y0=DATA[0].y,y1=DATA[DATA.length-1].y;
  var vals=DATA.map(function(d){return d.gf;}).concat(DATA.map(function(d){return d.bf;}));
  var vMin=Math.min.apply(null,vals)-1.0, vMax=Math.max.apply(null,vals)+1.0;
  function xs(y){return mL+(y-y0)/(y1-y0)*iw;}
  function ysc(v){return mT+ih-(v-vMin)/(vMax-vMin)*ih;}
  function pts(key){return DATA.map(function(d){return xs(d.y)+','+ysc(d[key]);}).join(' ');}
  var s='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+W+' '+H+'" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Median first-marriage age by year, grooms and brides. Interactive: hover a point for its exact value.">';
  s+='<text x="10" y="16" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Median first-marriage age, 2003 to 2024 (hover a point)</text>';
  s+='<polyline points="'+pts('gf')+'" fill="none" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="2.4"/>';
  s+='<polyline points="'+pts('bf')+'" fill="none" stroke="#b5651d" stroke-width="2.4"/>';
  DATA.forEach(function(d){
    ['gf','bf'].forEach(function(key){
      var col=(key==='gf'?'#2f4b7c':'#b5651d');
      s+='<circle class="a1-pt" data-y="'+d.y+'" data-gf="'+d.gf+'" data-bf="'+d.bf+'" cx="'+xs(d.y)+'" cy="'+ysc(d[key])+'" r="7" fill="'+col+'" opacity="0" style="cursor:pointer;"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+xs(d.y)+'" cy="'+ysc(d[key])+'" r="2.6" fill="'+col+'"/>';
    });
  });
  s+='<text x="'+(W-14)+'" y="'+(ysc(DATA[DATA.length-1].gf)-8)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="10" fill="#2f4b7c" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Grooms</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+(W-14)+'" y="'+(ysc(DATA[DATA.length-1].bf)+16)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="10" fill="#b5651d" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Brides</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+mL+'" y="'+(H-6)+'" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">'+y0+'</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+(W-mR)+'" y="'+(H-6)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">'+y1+'</text>';
  s+='</svg>';
  document.getElementById('a1-chart-wrap').innerHTML=s;
  document.querySelectorAll('#a1-chart-wrap .a1-pt').forEach(function(c){
    c.addEventListener('mousemove',function(e){
      showTip(e, '<b>'+c.getAttribute('data-y')+'</b><br>Grooms: '+c.getAttribute('data-gf')+'<br>Brides: '+c.getAttribute('data-bf'));
    });
    c.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTip);
  });
})();
</script>
```

The original chart hides this.
Four overlapping lines lead the eye to read one shared slope, when there are really two different ones.
:::
::::::

::: small
Method: `lm(median_age ~ year)` per gender, 22 annual observations each.
Significance of both slopes and of their difference confirmed by two-sided *t*-tests; 95% CIs from the OLS standard errors.
:::

## A2: First Marriage and Re-marriage Are Drifting Further Apart {.smaller}

A linear regression of each derived gap column on year.
This gap is the connector label on every dumbbell, so A2 measures exactly what the reader sees.

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: box
**Both gaps widen, and both trends are significant.** Groom gap grows from **11.1 to 13.9 years** (slope 0.14 years/year, 95% CI 0.11–0.17; R² 0.80; *p* \< .001).
Bride gap grows from **7.6 to 10.0 years** (slope 0.10 years/year, 95% CI 0.08–0.12; R² 0.83; *p* \< .001).
:::

Re-marriage age is pulling away from first-marriage age for both genders.
The original chart never makes this point, because it never puts a number on the gap.
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div id="a2-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div>
<script>
(function(){
  // Gap columns derived from the shared source rather than re-typed, so they can't drift from the dumbbell chart.
  var DATA=MARRIAGE_DATA.map(function(d){
    return {y:d.y, gg:+(d.gr-d.gf).toFixed(1), bg:+(d.br-d.bf).toFixed(1)};
  });

  var y0=DATA[0].y,y1=DATA[DATA.length-1].y;
  var vals=DATA.map(function(d){return d.gg;}).concat(DATA.map(function(d){return d.bg;}));
  var vMin=Math.min.apply(null,vals)-1.0, vMax=Math.max.apply(null,vals)+1.0;
  function xs(y){return mL+(y-y0)/(y1-y0)*iw;}
  function ysc(v){return mT+ih-(v-vMin)/(vMax-vMin)*ih;}
  function pts(key){return DATA.map(function(d){return xs(d.y)+','+ysc(d[key]);}).join(' ');}
  var s='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+W+' '+H+'" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Groom and bride gap between first marriage and re-marriage age, by year. Interactive: hover a point for its exact value.">';
  s+='<text x="10" y="16" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Gap: re-marriage age minus first-marriage age (hover a point)</text>';
  s+='<polyline points="'+pts('gg')+'" fill="none" stroke="#2f4b7c" stroke-width="2.4"/>';
  s+='<polyline points="'+pts('bg')+'" fill="none" stroke="#b5651d" stroke-width="2.4"/>';
  DATA.forEach(function(d){
    ['gg','bg'].forEach(function(key){
      var col=(key==='gg'?'#2f4b7c':'#b5651d');
      s+='<circle class="a2-pt" data-y="'+d.y+'" data-gg="'+d.gg+'" data-bg="'+d.bg+'" cx="'+xs(d.y)+'" cy="'+ysc(d[key])+'" r="7" fill="'+col+'" opacity="0" style="cursor:pointer;"/>';
      s+='<circle cx="'+xs(d.y)+'" cy="'+ysc(d[key])+'" r="2.6" fill="'+col+'"/>';
    });
  });
  s+='<text x="'+(W-14)+'" y="'+(ysc(DATA[DATA.length-1].gg)-8)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="10" fill="#2f4b7c" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Groom gap</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+(W-14)+'" y="'+(ysc(DATA[DATA.length-1].bg)+16)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="10" fill="#b5651d" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Bride gap</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+mL+'" y="'+(H-6)+'" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">'+y0+'</text>';
  s+='<text x="'+(W-mR)+'" y="'+(H-6)+'" text-anchor="end" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">'+y1+'</text>';
  s+='</svg>';
  document.getElementById('a2-chart-wrap').innerHTML=s;
  document.querySelectorAll('#a2-chart-wrap .a2-pt').forEach(function(c){

    });
    c.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTip);

</script>
```
:::
::::::

::: small
Method: `lm(gap ~ year)` per gender, 22 annual observations each; 95% CIs from OLS standard errors.
The lower R² here than in A1 is expected: re-marriages are far fewer, so their annual medians react more to short-term shocks.
Both trends still clear *p* \< .001.
:::

## A3: Grooms and Brides Are Closing Their Age Gap {.smaller}

The year-by-year difference between groom and bride first-marriage age, plus a Pearson correlation between the two series.

:::::: columns
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: {.box .slate-box}
Correlation **r = 0.95** (95% CI 0.89–0.98; *p* \< .001, *n* = 22)

Gender gap narrows from **2.5 to 1.5 years** (mean 2.1)
:::

The two series move together closely, yet the distance between them shrinks.
Both genders rise, so they stay correlated.
Brides rise faster, so the age difference slowly closes.
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div id="a3-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA=MARRIAGE_DATA; // shared source, defined once in the deck's <head>; this chart only reads .y/.gf/.bf
  var W=480,H=200,mL=34,mR=16,mT=26,mB=30,iw=W-mL-mR,ih=H-mT-mB;
  var gVals=DATA.map(function(d){return d.gf;}), bVals=DATA.map(function(d){return d.bf;});
  var gMin=Math.min.apply(null,gVals)-0.3, gMax=Math.max.apply(null,gVals)+0.3;
  var bMin=Math.min.apply(null,bVals)-0.3, bMax=Math.max.apply(null,bVals)+0.3;
  function xs(v){return mL+(v-gMin)/(gMax-gMin)*iw;}
  function ysc(v){return mT+ih-(v-bMin)/(bMax-bMin)*ih;}
  // least-squares fit of bride age on groom age, drawn as a visual aid for the r = 0.95 correlation
  var n=DATA.length, sx=0,sy=0,sxy=0,sxx=0;
  DATA.forEach(function(d){sx+=d.gf;sy+=d.bf;sxy+=d.gf*d.bf;sxx+=d.gf*d.gf;});
  var mSlope=(n*sxy-sx*sy)/(n*sxx-sx*sx), mInt=(sy-mSlope*sx)/n;
  var s='<svg viewBox="0 0 '+W+' '+H+'" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Groom median age plotted against bride median age, by year. Interactive: hover a point for its year.">';
  s+='<text x="10" y="16" font-size="11" fill="#23304a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" font-weight="600">Groom vs bride first-marriage age (hover a point)</text>';
  s+='<line x1="'+mL+'" y1="'+(H-mB)+'" x2="'+(W-mR)+'" y2="'+(H-mB)+'" stroke="#e4ddd2"/>';
  s+='<line x1="'+mL+'" y1="'+mT+'" x2="'+mL+'" y2="'+(H-mB)+'" stroke="#e4ddd2"/>';
  s+='<line x1="'+xs(gMin)+'" y1="'+ysc(mSlope*gMin+mInt)+'" x2="'+xs(gMax)+'" y2="'+ysc(mSlope*gMax+mInt)+'" stroke="#c8791f" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="4,3"/>';
  DATA.forEach(function(d){
    s+='<circle class="a3-pt" data-y="'+d.y+'" data-gf="'+d.gf+'" data-bf="'+d.bf+'" cx="'+xs(d.gf)+'" cy="'+ysc(d.bf)+'" r="7" fill="#3d5a80" opacity="0" style="cursor:pointer;"/>';
    s+='<circle cx="'+xs(d.gf)+'" cy="'+ysc(d.bf)+'" r="3.6" fill="#3d5a80"/>';
  });
  s+='<text x="'+(mL+iw/2)+'" y="'+(H-6)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif">Groom median age, low to high &rarr;</text>';
  s+='<text x="12" y="'+(mT+ih/2)+'" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#5f6b7a" font-family="Inter, sans-serif" transform="rotate(-90 12 '+(mT+ih/2)+')">Bride median age</text>';
  s+='</svg>';
  document.getElementById('a3-chart-wrap').innerHTML=s;
  document.querySelectorAll('#a3-chart-wrap .a3-pt').forEach(function(c){
    c.addEventListener('mousemove',function(e){
      showTip(e, '<b>'+c.getAttribute('data-y')+'</b><br>Groom: '+c.getAttribute('data-gf')+'<br>Bride: '+c.getAttribute('data-bf'));
    });
    c.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTip);
  });
})();
</script>
```
:::
::::::

## Findings and Limitations {.smaller}

::: box
**What the numbers say.** Singaporeans marry later, and the pace depends on both gender and marriage order.
Brides drive the first-marriage rise, climbing almost twice as fast as grooms (A1).
Re-marriage age is pulling further away from first-marriage age for both genders, not holding at a fixed distance (A2).
And even though grooms and brides move together closely (*r* = 0.95), the gap between them keeps narrowing, year on year (A3).
None of that is visible in a single-panel line chart with four labelled points; it only shows up once the data is re-plotted around the gap itself.
:::

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center;margin:2px 0 12px;">
  <div style="flex:1 1 170px;background:#eef1f7;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 12px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:11px;color:#5f6b7a;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">A1 &middot; Age rise per year</div>
    <div style="font-size:16px;font-weight:700;color:#2f4b7c;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">Brides 0.14 yr, grooms 0.07 yr</div>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1 1 170px;background:#eef1f7;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 12px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:11px;color:#5f6b7a;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">A2 &middot; Gap widening, 2003&ndash;2024</div>
    <div style="font-size:16px;font-weight:700;color:#2f4b7c;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">Grooms +2.8 yr, brides +2.4 yr</div>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1 1 170px;background:#eef1f7;border-radius:8px;padding:8px 12px;text-align:center;">
    <div style="font-size:11px;color:#5f6b7a;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">A3 &middot; Gender gap, 2003&ndash;2024</div>
    <div style="font-size:16px;font-weight:700;color:#2f4b7c;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;">2.5 yr &rarr; 1.5 yr</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.box .slate-box}
**Limitations, kept in view.** Three things temper the headline.
*Covid:* groom re-marriage age falls from 44.2 in 2019 to 42.4 in 2021, then recovers to 44.6 in 2022.
Re-marriages are few enough that their annual medians swing with registration disruption, so the 2020–2021 dip is annotated on the chart rather than smoothed away.
*Distribution panel scope:* it draws on age-band counts for all marriage orders combined, not split by first marriage versus re-marriage, so it describes that year's overall population rather than the exact series being plotted.
*Correlation, not causation:* A3's *r* = 0.95 says grooms' and brides' ages move together, not that one drives the other.
Both plausibly respond to the same underlying trend toward later marriage generally.
:::

## Conclusion {.smaller}

- We took one thread from a Mothership.SG report and rebuilt it around the number it left implicit: the **gap** between first and re-marriage age, turning an implicit read into the explicit subject of the chart.
- The interactive dumbbell fixes all six weaknesses of the original: it shows every year, labels every value, prints every gap, and replaces a four-line tangle with a clean gender toggle plus a linked distribution view.
- Three analyses turn the visual into defensible, statistically significant claims (all *p* \< .001): brides drive the first-marriage rise (A1), both gaps are widening (A2), and the genders move together while their gap closes (A3).
- Zooming out, the story still lines up with Singapore's broader "marrying later" narrative, but it identifies *who* is doing more of the delaying, which the original never could: brides, not grooms, and by a growing margin.

```{=html}
<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);gap:6px 14px;max-width:820px;margin:10px auto 4px;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;font-size:11.5px;color:#3a4356;">
  <div>&#10003; <b>W1</b> Lines hard to tell apart</div>
  <div>&#10003; <b>W2</b> Gender comparison buried</div>
  <div>&#10003; <b>W3</b> Sparse points, no lookup</div>
  <div>&#10003; <b>W4</b> Only median, no spread</div>
  <div>&#10003; <b>W5</b> Gap never shown</div>
  <div>&#10003; <b>W6</b> Colour-blind unsafe pairing</div>
</div>
```

::: box
Singaporeans are not rejecting marriage.
They are delaying it, and who delays the most is changing.
:::
